reason: The weighty bills are LGBT equality measures: banning conversion therapy for minors (rows 1,4,8,9,18,29), banning discrimination by sexual orientation or gender identity in housing, services, health care and law definitions (6,7,10-14,16,26,30,33,35,36), adoption and parenthood for same-sex couples (3,19,20,22,23,28,37,40), plus the right to equality in the Basic Law (2). The statement asks exactly this, and its price (religious providers, therapists and businesses constrained) matches what the anti-discrimination and conversion-therapy bills impose. Civil marriage / civil union bills (5,15,24,32, about 10% of weight) are broader than LGBT (they also cover couples barred from religious marriage) but they point the same way and are inside the direction's 'non-traditional families'; not enough to warrant a split.
